Triage: lands in `packages/services/service-automation` ⇒ `domain:services`. Graded `Bug` · `priority:p2`.

`Bug` by the mechanical boundary test: nothing widens. One branch is spelled on two calendars and the repair puts it on the one the sibling branch already uses.

### Why `p2` and not `p3`, and why not `p1`

**Against p3:** four of the six measured consumers **write a persisted date field** — a quote expiration, two followup dates, a close date, a due date. A query window one day wide is a sweep that misses a row; a **written** date is wrong data that outlives the run, and the card's sharpest line is that **nothing downstream can tell it was wrong**. That is a data-correctness defect, not a reporting one.

**Against p1:** the exposure is roughly one transition hour per DST-observing zone, twice a year, and the bare `{TODAY()}` form is unaffected. Narrow window, small fix.

⭐ **The reason it has survived is worth carrying into the dispatch**: local `setDate(getDate() + n)` shifts the instant by exactly n×24h whenever the local day is 24 hours long, so the mixed spelling is **accidentally equivalent** to UTC arithmetic on ordinary days. And CI runners sit at UTC, where the two spellings are **behaviourally indistinguishable**. ⇒ Nothing was ever going to go red on this.

### ⛔ The provenance fence is the most important thing on this card

The filing seat states plainly that it **did not independently verify the platform half** — the reading was taken by an `os-dev` agent against **installed 17.2.0**, reading the shipped `dist` and executing probes, because the hotcrm checkout has no `node_modules`. ⇒ **Re-take the reading on `origin/main` before writing any fix.** The honest current statement is *"reported and probed downstream, ⛔ not re-measured here"*, and triage has ⛔ not re-measured it either.

⚠️ What the seat **did** verify is the consumer side, directly on `objectstack-ai/hotcrm@main`: six live usages of the offset form, four of them writing dates. That half is measured.

### The guard note is a hard constraint, not advice

⛔ **A regression test for this cannot be written to run only at `TZ=UTC`** — the two spellings are indistinguishable there. It needs a DST-observing zone **and** an instant inside that zone's transition hour. A single-point sweep is exactly what cleared the downstream helper for months.

⭐ There is a ready-made reproduction shape next door: `objectstack-ai/hotcrm#1462` / PR `#1507` fixed the identical two-calendar shape in a test helper, with a 10-zone × 8-instant matrix (**6 red before, 0 after**, every red cell a DST zone at its own spring-forward hour) and a widened sweep over **34 zones × 595,680 pairs** (mixed spelling flips 47, single-calendar flips none). ⇒ Reuse the shape; ⛔ do not re-invent the harness.

### Two things ⛔ out of scope, stated by the card and upheld here

⛔ This does **not** change what `{TODAY()}` means — the bare form already resolves to the UTC day and consumers assert against that. The offset branch is being made to **agree** with it.
⛔ Whether these tokens should be timezone-aware at all is a separate, larger question. If a dev finds itself designing that, it has left this card.

## Landed — `6c439f2b43ffbab900900fc7e9d44036483e80ef`

PR [#15826](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/15826) is on `main`: `fix(service-automation): resolve `{TODAY() +/- n}` on one calendar, not two (#14852) (#15826)`.

Landing authority is `git log origin/main | grep -c '(#15826)'` = 1, with `(#15365)` = 1 as the cwd control. ⚠️ For anyone reading this later: **do not read the commit's date as the landing time.** This commit carries `09:46:57Z`, but `git merge-base --is-ancestor` puts it *outside* `origin/main` as late as `10:31:53Z` and inside it by `10:38:45Z`. The date is when the merge queue built the candidate, not when the candidate reached `main` — ~55 min after auto-merge was armed at 09:40Z, ordinary for the observed queue band.

`pm:dispatched` stripped; the card keeps `bug`, `priority:p2`, `domain:services`, read back to confirm.

### The fix

One line in `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/template.ts`:

```diff
-        if (offset) now.setDate(now.getDate() + sign * offset);
+        if (offset) now.setUTCDate(now.getUTCDate() + sign * offset);
```

`{TODAY() + n}` was reading the day on the **local** calendar and writing it back on the same setter while the rest of the expression resolved in UTC, so the two calendars disagreed across a DST boundary and the resolved date came out one day off.

### ⚠️ One thing the changeset does not fully state — carry it into release-note work

The changeset states only the `+n` half of the direction rule. **The complete rule, measured across the sweep (94 of 96 cases), is:**

| local-vs-UTC slack | offset | outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **−1 h** | `+n` (spring) **or** `−n` (fall) | resolves **EARLY** |
| **+1 h** | `+n` (fall) **or** `−n` (spring) | resolves **LATE** |

The direction of the error is decided by the **sign of the slack combined with the sign of the offset**, not by the offset alone. A release note written from the changeset text alone would describe half the defect. This is recorded here rather than as a changeset amendment because release notes are written centrally at release time — ⛔ never accreted a row per PR.

This card's own history is worth keeping as a pattern: **the card's framing was inverted, the dev's correction was right for `+n` only, and the contract review completed it.** Each step was right about what it measured and incomplete about what it did not — which is the argument for the review round, not against the dev.
